chunks: And the Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb. And he informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abū al-Numayr, the mawlā of al-Ḥārith ibn al-Mughīrah al-Naḍrī, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Tell me about the young boy—up to what age may women wash him? He said: “Up to three years.”

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the source of the ruling
key_terms.الصَّبِيِّ: the young boy or minor child being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.النِّسَاءُ: women, who are the subject of the legal ruling
key_terms.تُغَسِّلُهُ: wash him ritually, referring here to washing the deceased body
key_terms.ثَلَاثِ سِنِينَ: three years, the stated age limit in this narration

ai.seo_question: Up to what age may women wash the body of a deceased young boy in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning the washing of a deceased young boy by women. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that women may wash him up to the age of three years, indicating a legal age limit in funerary washing.
